relevance_note: Yes, but only one person: an adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD) cohort screened by NGS in which one patient (Patient 4) carries a TNFAIP3 variant classed as a VUS, 'in another patient in TNFAIP3 (c.1939A>C)'; the authors do not diagnose HA20 in anyone.
method_note: Read the whole paper; values entered by hand, and Table 2 spans cut from the row text by a short script, then every span checked verbatim against the paper. Individuals: the five patients individually described in Table 2 (Patients 1-5, all with VUS). Only Patient 4 has a TNFAIP3 variant; Patients 1-2 (NOD2), 3 (TNFRSF1A) and 5 (SCN9A) are included because they are individually described, so downstream should filter on gene. The other 19 cohort patients appear only in aggregate (Table 1) and have no rows. Ages: Table 2 gives each patient an age (e.g. 'Female, 60 years') without saying whether it is age at diagnosis, onset or report; left as not reported in all age fields (context: Table 1 reports only 'Age at diagnosis', range 18-70). Ages printed for Patients 1-5: 48, 49, 18, 60 and 19 years. Protein strings come from Table 3 ('Present study' column), printed without 'p.' and in one-letter code; attributed only where a gene has a single carrier (TNFAIP3: T647P -> Patient 4; TNFRSF1A: P75L -> Patient 3; SCN9A: G884S -> Patient 5). NOD2 'R675W, E751K' were not attributed because only list order links them to Patients 1 and 2. Not reconciled: simple codon arithmetic on the printed cDNA (c.2104 -> codon 702, c.2617 -> codon 873) does not match R675W or G884S, which may reflect a different transcript or an error; no transcript is printed. Zygosity, inheritance, parental testing and variant class are not stated for anyone. Group statements used: 'all patients had elevated acute-phase reactant levels and hyperferritinemia' applied as observed to each of the five (inferred from group statement); 'Positive ANCA ... 0 (0)' is a count only and was not used to exclude. 'Fever' was not mapped to the checklist item 'recurrent fever' (recurrence not stated). Severe sicca syndrome (Patient 2) was not mapped to ocular inflammation, and leukopenia (Patient 5) not to autoimmune cytopenia (not stated as autoimmune). Narrative counts not linked to named patients (anterior uveitis n=2, headache n=2, posterior leukoencephalopathy n=1, mucocutaneous ulcers 6/24, one patient with affected relatives) were not attributed. Statements that Patient 4 'did not show atypical symptoms' and was classed into AOSD cluster 2 ('uncomplicated') were not recorded as features. Possible inconsistency: the Discussion says both NOD2 patients 'were refractory to conventional DMARDs', but Table 2 lists no conventional DMARD for Patient 1 (GC, NSAIDs, colchicine, etanercept). The Discussion spells the gene 'TNFAIP' once.
